root_motivation: CLAUDE_SELF.md is the negotiated contract between user and agent — the *diffs* are the portrait. Phase 1a extracts every commit's hash/date/diff-hunk/message into structured JSON so downstream rendering passes (Claude reflections, Typst typesetting, A2 print) can consume a stable contract. Until the extractor exists, no later artifact can be built or audited.
user_persona: jsy running it against the wintermute CLAUDE_SELF.md (`/home/jsy/wintermute/dotfiles/.claude/CLAUDE_SELF.md` or wherever the file lives in dotfiles). Audience for the JSON: the next pipeline stage (reflection generator) and the human eye spot-checking that diffs round-trip cleanly.

unfakeable_metric.name: acceptance_tests_passing
unfakeable_metric.harness_command: cargo test --tests 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok' | wc -l

acceptance_criteria.description: `self-portrait extract --file <repo-relative-path> [--repo <dir>]` emits a single JSON object on stdout: `{file, repo, generated_at, commits: [...]}`. Each commit entry has: hash (full sha), short_hash (7 chars), author_name, author_email, committed_at (RFC3339), subject, body, diff (unified diff hunk for this file across this commit, file headers stripped). Order: oldest commit first.
Follows file renames via git's --follow semantics — a commit that renamed the file appears in the commits array, with `diff` containing the rename hunk.

Commits that touched the file with a trivial change (no semantic diff after the rename) still appear and their `diff` is included verbatim; the consumer decides whether to collapse them. The extractor does not editorialize.

When the file does not exist in the current HEAD but did historically (e.g. it was deleted), the extractor still walks the history — exits 0 with all commits in `commits` and a top-level `"deleted_at": "<RFC3339>"` field. If the file never existed under any name, exits with code 3 and stderr containing the path and `no commits found`.
When `--repo <dir>` points at a non-git path: exit code 2 with stderr containing the path and `not a git repository`.

Commit messages with `private: true` in a Markdown-style trailer line (e.g. line `private: true` at column 0) cause the diff hunk for that commit to be redacted to the string `"[redacted]"`. The hash/date/author/subject still appear so the timeline is complete. This honours the PRD's privacy clause.

`--collapse-trivial` collapses commits whose `diff` body, after stripping whitespace/comments, is empty into a single virtual `{hash: "trivial", subject: "N trivial edits", ...}` adjacent entry; default is no collapse (AC3).

scope: Walk git log --follow of one file under a repo
Per-commit: hash, short hash, author name+email, committed_at, subject, body, the file's diff hunk
Mark deleted-then-revived files via deleted_at field
Honour private:true trailer in commit message → diff redaction
Emit single JSON object on stdout
non_goals: Reflection generation (LLM-call producing 1–2 sentence per-commit narrative) — Phase 1b
Typst, paged.js, PDF, SVG, or any rendering

five_whys_trace.q: Why a JSON extractor as Phase 1a, separate from reflection + Typst rendering?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the reflection stage is the only one that requires the model — and it's iterative on taste. Separating the deterministic git walk lets reflections be re-run against a frozen extract, and lets the typesetting be re-run against a frozen extract + reflections, without re-walking git each time.

five_whys_trace.q: Why include the raw diff verbatim rather than parsed AST or summary?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the print panel shows the diff itself with subtle green/red highlighting — the diff is artwork, not data. A summary would lose the typographic texture that the print is built around.

five_whys_trace.q: Why honour private:true trailers in this stage rather than a later filter?
five_whys_trace.a: Because privacy is the contract — a redacted diff should never leave this stage in unredacted form, regardless of downstream consumer bugs. Privacy must be enforced at the source of truth.
